I got burned by a new hard disk that failed. It took down my complete OS and all my backups were corrupt, so I had to reinstall everything.

Fast forwards: Months later OS is separated from my data drive, NAS backup and external backup drive of that NAS drive. And on top of that regular clones of my OS drive.

I am now migrating to a new PC (MSI Z170A XPower Gaming Titanium) that has RAID included.

Now comes the question:

* Is it worth to have the Windows 10 OS hard disks configured as a Raid 1/5? * Is it easy to start with a RAID 0 disk OS only, then in a later stage, migrate to RAID 1 or maybe 5 easily? * Will I get boot issues when my OS starts in RAID 1? * Assume that one of the hard disks in RAID 1 fail, will I be able to start up my OS easily?

I am spoiled with a NAS drive that automatically expands disk space and and re balances my data, but that can take weeks. Will I get the same with the motherboard RAID?

The questions are for Windows 10 but when I migrate to Linux (end goal in a few years). how will that affect Linux?

What are your experiences and feedback?
Motherboard RAID controllers and your OS questions.

Do your research on how easy it is to repair a broken RAID 1. A few years back i was using a software based RAID 1, when one HDD failed it gave me an error message that it is broken, but would still boot just fine. Replaced the broken HDD, booted up and then simple selected repair RAID 1, and everything copied over in the background.
My current motherboard supports on board RAID controller. One hard drive failed, i could still boot no problem, but when i replaced the broken HDD and attempted to repair the array, it simply wiped out everything ( yes i replaced the correct HDD). I had to recover everything important from my secondary backup a external HDD.

This is exactly why I ask the question.

The intention is not to bother to backup everything and then restore. In the case of my NAS, I just insert a new hard-disk and everything gets synchronized (can take days).

But it is interesting that you still could boot up with only one hard disk.

One of the things I am a bit scared of, is when I have an OS, that the crippled drive starts to corrupt the good hard-disk by overwriting bad data.
